newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST - Caution to mark Portugal 10-yr bond sale.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Caution to mark Portugal 10-yr bond sale.

text.p: Bids at the Portuguese sale of 25 billion escudos of 10-year bonds were seen above the 6.55 percent at which the secondary market closed on Monday, raising the prospect of the Institute for Public Credit Management's opting not to place all the paper, analysts said.
At the last offer of the February 2007 paper on May 6, the average yield was 6.6838 percent.
"The doubt is about how much the Institute will place. Whether it places just part of the 25 billion escudos or even anything at all," said one trader.
The result is due around 1000 GMT.
"I am going to put some bids at 6.60 percent but the biggest amounts I will put closer to 6.70 percent," said one fixed-income trader.
International bond markets have been unsettled by the leftwing victory in French elections and the row between Bonn and the Bundesbank over the revaluation of gold reserves.
Both developments appear to cast doubt over Europe's plans for monetary union in 1999, or at least the form in which it may be launched.
